newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP, CRA sag as metals soften.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP, CRA sag as metals soften.

text.p: Shares in resource leaders the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and CRA Ltd sagged under the weight of softer metals prices on Wednesday, the rout exacerbated by a strong Australian dollar and generally weaker short term outlook for both companies.
By 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT), BHP shares were 49 cents lower at A$16.11 after reaching an intraday low of A$16.04, while CRA shares were 54 cents lower at A$18.42, off an intraday low of A$18.32.
Both shares saw active trade, BHP seeing turnover of 6.4 million shares, while CRA saw 2.5 million shares traded.
Brokers said BHP had been hit by a combination of profit downgrades and pessimistic comments from its managing director John Prescott on Tuesday.
"You saw profit downgrades from Were and Macintosh and Prescott's comments on Tuesday," said dealer Glen Morgan of Daiwa Securities.
The profit downgrades were due to concerns about weaker copper prices impacting on BHP's bottom line. Prescott has said the company faces a real challenge over the copper price.
